events.memory: User recalls a conversation with a Red facilities employee about an all-hands meeting, which might provide a lead to the file number.
User considers using the walky-talky to ask for help or information, or to reach out to Red again.
User remembers a designation for the study on their jumpsuit and a mention of the previous iteration of the study on a clipboard.
User recalls the designation 'LIV' on their jumpsuit and a mention of an aberration in the previous iteration on a clipboard.
User focuses on searching for a file related to the 'LIV' designation, specifically looking for any mention of an aberration in the previous iteration.
Files are numbered in Arabic numerals, into the hundreds and maybe even thousands.
I consider the possibility that LIV might indicate a number itself and realize it is the Roman numeral for 54.
I start searching for file number 54 in the records room.
I find record 54, which has the name A on it and says, EXPERIMENT IN PROGRESS.
I open file 54 to find more information about the experiment labeled 'A' and why it's still in progress.
I wonder what the previous iteration's aberration means, given the instruction to examine the file for details.
I press the GREEN button on the walky-talky, hoping it will provide information about the location of security or how to get there.
I reply to the security voice on the walky-talky, asking for directions to the security room.
The security voice is gruff and suspicious, telling me to follow green pipes to security.
I decide to follow the green pipes in the hallway to find the security room.
I am cautious not to wander too much, using my square pill powers to navigate back to known locations.
I decide to go back to Room LIV, the location where I initially noticed the colored pipes.
The green pipe leads to the security room, which has a security panel with a green slash.
I use a keycard with a green stripe to enter the security room.
The security room contains a control panel with monitors labeled NARCO CHAMBERS.
I examine the control panel and monitors labeled NARCO CHAMBERS to find any useful information.
There are three chambers, marked Chamber 1, Chamber 2, and Chamber 3, each with three sticky pads and a note.
A password screen with a keyboard asking for a 5-letter password is located on the right.
I examine the sticky pads and notes on each chamber to find a clue for the password.
